definition_zh: 欣赏；享受；喜欢；玩得愉快
definition_en: to get pleasure from something, or to have a good time
core_image: 嘴角上扬的人：把快乐从一件事里一口一口吃出来
scene: 阳光洒进院子，奶奶端出热茶，笑着说慢慢喝。We sat in the garden and enjoyed the warm sunshine and good tea.
sceneCN: 这里 enjoy 是「享受、欣赏」（第 1 个义项：从某事物中获得快乐）；句意是我们在花园里享受阳光与好茶。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -able 后缀构成，义为「令人愉快的」
由动词加 -ment 后缀构成，义为「乐趣；享受」
由形容词加 -ly 后缀构成，义为「愉快地」

senses.title: To get pleasure from something
senses.definition: to take delight or pleasure in something you do, see, eat or hear
senses.definitionCN: 从自己做、看、吃或听的事情中获得快乐
senses.example: I enjoy listening to jazz after work.
senses.exampleCN: 我喜欢下班后听爵士乐。
senses.why: The prefix en- means to put into, and joy is the pleasure itself, so the verb pictures putting yourself inside the joy.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 en- 表示「使进入」，joy 就是快乐本身，动词画面是把自己放进快乐里面。

senses.title: To have a good time
senses.definition: to spend time in a way that gives you pleasure, often in the phrase enjoy oneself
senses.definitionCN: 度过一段带来快乐的时光，常用短语 enjoy oneself
senses.example: The children enjoyed themselves at the amusement park.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们在游乐园玩得很开心。
senses.why: When the object is yourself, the image turns inward: you are the thing being filled with joy.
senses.whyCN: 当宾语是自己时，画面转向内部：你自己就是被快乐填满的那个对象。

senses.title: To be in a favourable state or position
senses.definition: to be in a situation that gives you an advantage, such as good health or fame
senses.definitionCN: 处于某种有利的状态或地位，如健康、名声
senses.example: The company enjoys a good reputation among customers.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司在顾客中享有好口碑。
senses.why: A good situation is like a dish you keep tasting, so the pleasure verb stretches to mean having something pleasant.
senses.whyCN: 好的处境就像让你不断尝到甜头的菜，于是快乐动词延伸出「享有」的意思。

intro.en: Enjoy comes through Old French and Anglo-French from a late Latin verb about bringing joy to someone. It entered English in the fourteenth century and later turned inward to mean taking pleasure oneself.
intro.cn: enjoy 经古法语与英式法语，来自晚期拉丁语一个表示「使某人喜悦」的动词。它于十四世纪进入英语，后来转向内部，表示自己获得快乐。

items.en: The late Latin verb gaudere meant 'to rejoice', and its causative form meant 'to make someone rejoice'.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语动词 gaudere 意为「欣喜」，其使动形式意为「使某人欣喜」。

items.en: Old French enjoier meant 'to give joy to, to rejoice'. The en- prefix carried the sense of putting joy into a person.
items.cn: 古法语 enjoier 意为「给予快乐、欣喜」。前缀 en- 带有「把快乐放进人心里」的意思。

items.en: English borrowed the word in the late fourteenth century as enjoien, meaning 'to rejoice or celebrate'.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪末借入 enjoien，意为「欣喜、庆祝」。

items.en: In the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries the sense shifted to taking pleasure for oneself, giving the modern use enjoy the meal.
items.cn: 十五、十六世纪词义转向为自己获得快乐，形成现代用法 enjoy the meal。

items.en: The reflexive phrase enjoy oneself became common in the seventeenth century and now names having a good time.
items.cn: 反身短语 enjoy oneself 在十七世纪变得常用，如今专指玩得开心。

note.en: The first group collects words built on the same joy root; the second collects near meanings about pleasure.
note.cn: 第一组收集同一 joy 词根的词；第二组收集与「快乐」相关的近义词。

entries.definition: giving pleasure; pleasant to do or experience
entries.definitionCN: 令人愉快的；好受的。由 enjoy 加 -able 构成。

entries.definition: the state or feeling of taking pleasure in something
entries.definitionCN: 乐趣；享受。由 enjoy 加 -ment 构成的名词。

entries.definition: in a way that gives pleasure
entries.definitionCN: 愉快地。由形容词 enjoyable 加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: to find something pleasant or agreeable, a plainer everyday word
entries.definitionCN: 喜欢；觉得好。更朴素的日常用词，感情强度较弱。

entries.definition: to recognize the value of something and feel grateful or pleased
entries.definitionCN: 欣赏；感激。强调认识到价值，比 enjoy 更郑重。

entries.definition: to enjoy slowly and fully, usually about taste or moments
entries.definitionCN: 细细品味。强调放慢速度、充分体会，多用于味道或时刻。

normalIntro.en: Five concrete hooks built from the real word family and daily phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 五条基于真实词族与日常搭配的具体联想。

normal.en: en- means put into, joy is the pleasure: putting joy inside your heart is enjoying.
normal.cn: en-（使进入）+ joy（快乐）：把快乐装进心里，就是享受。

normal.en: The joy family: joyful, joyous and enjoy share one root.
normal.cn: joy 系词族：joyful 快乐的、joyous 喜悦的、enjoy 享受，同根好记。

normal.en: Enjoy your meal is the phrase every restaurant uses.
normal.cn: Enjoy your meal! 餐厅最常听见的一句话，点菜时自然记住。

normal.en: Enjoy oneself means having fun; the joy returns to yourself.
normal.cn: Enjoy oneself = 玩得开心，主语是自己，快乐回到自己身上。

normal.en: The sound hints at yin joy: pulling joy in, which helps spelling only.
normal.cn: 谐音：音近「引 joy」——把 joy 引进来，帮助拼读，不是词源。

abstract.en: Picture a winter night by the fire, holding hot cocoa and smiling.
abstract.cn: 画面：冬夜暖炉旁，你捧着热可可，嘴角慢慢上扬。

abstract.en: Imagine joy as a candy and en- as putting it into your mouth.
abstract.cn: 动作：把快乐想象成一颗糖，en- 是把糖放进嘴里。

abstract.en: A day well enjoyed feels like a sun-dried quilt, fluffy and warm.
abstract.cn: 感觉：enjoy 过的一天像被阳光晒过的被子，蓬松温暖。

examples.en: I enjoy reading novels on rainy afternoons.
examples.cn: 我喜欢在下雨的午后读小说。

examples.en: We enjoyed ourselves at the school sports day.
examples.cn: 我们在学校运动会上玩得很开心。

examples.en: A light dinner can be enjoyable after a long day.
examples.cn: 漫长一天之后，简单的晚餐也会令人愉快。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因joy」——因为 joy（快乐）而喜欢，谐音帮助拼读，不是词源。

root: enjoy 由前缀 en-（使进入）+ 词根 joy（快乐，源自拉丁语 gaudere 的古法语形式 joie）构成，字面即「使进入快乐」。词根 jo- 在英语 joy、rejoice、joyful 中同源。

sensesIntro.en: Enjoy moves from taking pleasure in things, to having a good time yourself, to being in a fortunate situation.
sensesIntro.cn: enjoy 从享受事物，到自己过得愉快，再到处于有利的境况，三层义项层层外扩。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: putting yourself inside a moment of joy.
core.cn: 核心意象：把自己放进一个快乐的时刻里。

branches.cn: 从食物、音乐、爱好与时刻中获得快乐。
enjoy oneself 与他人同乐。
享有健康、名声或好口碑，如同细细品尝。
常常因分享而生长的个人喜悦。
对已拥有之物的安静欣赏。

intro.en: Enjoy is built from a Latin root through French, and its family keeps the joy core visible.
intro.cn: enjoy 经法语源自拉丁语词根，其词族始终围绕 joy 核心。

latinIntro.en: Latin gaudere 'rejoice' is the shared ancestor behind this family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 gaudere「欣喜」是这一词族的共同祖先。

items.example: enable means to make able.
She cried with joy at the news.
enjoyable means causing enjoyment.
enjoyment is the state of enjoying.
enjoyably means in an enjoyable way.

items.meaning: to feel or show great joy
items.example: They rejoiced at the victory.
a joyful wedding day
Reading gives her great enjoyment.
items.exampleCN: 读书给她带来极大的乐趣。

definition_zh: 足够的；充足的；足够地；相当；够了
definition_en: as much or as many as is needed; to the necessary degree
core_image: 装满的水杯：水位刚好到需要的刻度线
scene: 水壶咕嘟作响，妈妈看着杯子水线到了刻度。There is enough hot water for everyone's tea.
sceneCN: 这里 enough 是「足够的」（第 1 个义项：数量达到需要）；句意是热水够每个人泡茶。

derivatives.zh: 较罕见派生词，义为「充足状态；够用」
加否定前缀 in- 的形容词，义为「不足的」（由 sufficient 变形）

senses.title: As much as is needed
senses.definition: as much or as many of something as is required
senses.definitionCN: 数量或程度达到所需要的量
senses.example: We have enough chairs for all the guests.
senses.exampleCN: 我们的椅子够所有客人坐。
senses.why: The word comes from a Germanic root meaning to reach or suffice, so the image is a container filled to the needed line.
senses.whyCN: 该词来自日耳曼语词根，意为「达到、满足」，画面是容器刚好装到需要的刻度。

senses.title: To the necessary degree
senses.titleCN: 足够地；达到需要的程度
senses.definition: to the degree that something is necessary or wanted
senses.definitionCN: 达到必要或期望的程度
senses.example: He is old enough to travel alone.
senses.exampleCN: 他年龄够大，可以独自旅行。
senses.why: Used after adjectives, enough measures how far a quality has climbed up the scale toward the needed mark.
senses.whyCN: enough 放在形容词后，衡量某种性质沿刻度爬到所需位置的程度。

senses.title: Quite or rather
senses.definition: fairly or to a noticeable degree, often to soften a remark
senses.definitionCN: 相当的程度，常用来缓和语气
senses.example: The film was interesting enough, but not exciting.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影还算有趣，但不刺激。
senses.why: A full cup can still be just ordinary, so enough also works as a mild degree word.
senses.whyCN: 满杯也可能只是平平无奇，于是 enough 也可以作程度温和的副词。

senses.title: A sufficient amount
senses.definition: the amount that is needed; as much as necessary
senses.definitionCN: 所需的数量；必需的量
senses.example: Enough has been said about the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 关于这个计划说得够多了。
senses.why: When the thing itself is left unstated, enough stands alone as a noun for the filled measure.
senses.whyCN: 当所谈之物不必点明时，enough 单独作名词，代表那满刻度的量。

intro.en: Enough comes from Old English about filling or reaching a measure. It is a purely Germanic word with close cousins in other Germanic languages.
intro.cn: enough 来自古英语，与「填满、达到量度」有关。它是纯粹的日耳曼语词，在其他日耳曼语言中有近亲。

items.en: The reconstructed root meant 'to reach, to suffice', seen in related Germanic words for content and sufficiency.
items.cn: 重构的日耳曼语词根意为「达到、满足」，见于表示满足、充足的日耳曼语同族词。

items.en: Old English genoh meant 'enough, in sufficient quantity', built from ge- (together) plus the root nah.
items.cn: 古英语 genoh 意为「足够、数量充分」，由 ge-（一起）加词根 nah 构成。

items.en: Middle English spelled it inoh and enow, and the plural enow survived in poetry for 'enough people'.
items.cn: 中古英语拼写为 inoh 和 enow，复数 enow 在诗歌里留存，表示「足够多的人」。

items.en: The modern form enough fixed its spelling in the fifteenth century, keeping the silent gh from the older pronunciation.
items.cn: 现代拼写 enough 在十五世纪定型，gh 不发音，保留了古音的痕迹。

items.en: The idiom sure enough, meaning 'as expected', is recorded from the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 习语 sure enough「果然」最早见于十七世纪的记录。

note.en: The first group collects Germanic look-alikes with the same shape; the second collects near meanings about sufficiency.
note.cn: 第一组收集形近的日耳曼语词；第二组收集与「充足」相关的近义词。

entries.definition: an old plural form of enough, now found only in literature
entries.definitionCN: enough 的古体复数，如今只见于文学作品。

entries.definition: comfortable and warm; only similar in ending, not related in root
entries.definitionCN: 温暖舒适的；只是词尾拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: a conjunction meaning although; shares the -ough letter pattern but not the root
entries.definitionCN: 虽然；共有 -ough 拼写模式，但词源不同。

entries.definition: formal word for as much as is needed
entries.definitionCN: 足够的（正式用语）。多用于书面语。

entries.definition: more than enough, often large in size or amount
entries.definitionCN: 充裕的；丰富的。强调超出需要。

entries.definition: just enough for the purpose, sometimes barely so
entries.definitionCN: 够用的；勉强够的。强调达到基本要求。

normalIntro.en: Five concrete hooks built from spelling, sound and real usage.
normalIntro.cn: 五条基于拼写、读音与真实用法的具体联想。

normal.en: e plus nough: nough sounds like a need that stops complaining once served.
normal.cn: e + nough：nough 谐音「闹服」——需求被满足，闹够了就服了。

normal.en: Compare old enough to go: enough follows the adjective.
normal.cn: 对比例句：old enough to go（够大能去），enough 在形容词后面。

normal.en: Learn sure enough and not enough as a positive-negative pair.
normal.cn: sure enough 果然；not enough 不够，一正一反成对记。

normal.en: Enough matches German genug; the g corresponds to gh.
normal.cn: enough 与 German 里的 genug 同源，g 对应 gh，德英对照好记。

normal.en: The sound hints at taking once and having enough, for spelling only.
normal.cn: 谐音：「一拿 enough」——一拿就够，帮助拼读，不是词源。

abstract.en: Picture the water level stopping exactly on the dotted line.
abstract.cn: 画面：杯中水位刚好停在虚线上，一滴不多一滴不少。

abstract.en: Feel the moment you put down your chopsticks, full and done.
abstract.cn: 感觉：吃饱后放下筷子的那一刻，身体说 enough。

abstract.en: Draw a line in the air; where the line lands is the needed amount.
abstract.cn: 动作：伸手指在空中画一条线，线到之处就是需要的量。

examples.en: There is not enough milk for breakfast.
examples.cn: 牛奶不够早餐用的。

examples.en: She is tall enough to reach the top shelf.
examples.cn: 她个子够高，能够到最上层的架子。

examples.en: Sure enough, the train arrived on time.
examples.cn: 果然，火车准时到达。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「闹夫」——不闹了，丈夫总算把东西拿够，谐音帮助拼读，不是词源。

root: enough 来自古英语 genōh（ge- 表完成 + nōh「达到、满足」），与德语 genug、荷兰语 genoeg 同源，是纯粹的日耳曼语词，与拉丁语系词根无关。

sensesIntro.en: Enough works as adjective, adverb and noun, all around the single image of a measure that is filled to the mark.
sensesIntro.cn: enough 可作形容词、副词与名词，全部围绕「量器装到刻度线」这一个意象展开。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a container filled exactly to the needed line.
core.cn: 核心意象：容器刚好装到所需刻度线。

branches.cn: 足够的椅子、足够的钱、足够的某物。
old enough、strong enough，放在形容词之后。
interesting enough 表示温和、公允的评价。
名词省略时单独使用的 enough。
不再需要更多的共同感受。

intro.en: Enough is a single Germanic word; its family lives in Germanic languages, not Latin.
intro.cn: enough 是单个日耳曼语词；其词族在日耳曼语言中，不在拉丁语中。

latinIntro.en: No Latin root applies; the family is Germanic, so the Latin entry list is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 本词与拉丁词根无关，词族属于日耳曼语，因此拉丁同源词列表为空。

items.example: In genoh the prefix marked the goal being reached.
items.exampleCN: 在 genoh 中该前缀表示目标达成。

items.example: though, through and enough share the silent gh spelling.
items.exampleCN: though、through 与 enough 共享不发音的 gh。

items.example: Sufficient literally means held up to the need.
The same root appears in factory and efficient.
items.exampleCN: 该词根也见于 factory 与 efficient。

items.example: Ample means wide enough to hold more than needed.
Adequate means equal to the task.
Insufficient means not sufficient.
Genug mirrors Old English genoh almost exactly.
items.exampleCN: genug 与古英语 genoh 几乎完全对应。

definition_zh: 进入；参加；报名参加；输入（数据）；走进
definition_en: to go or come into a place; to take part in; to put information into a system
core_image: 跨过门槛：从外面一步走进里面
scene: 校门口闸机打开，学生刷卡走进考场。The students entered the exam room one by one.
sceneCN: 这里 enter 是「进入」（第 1 个义项：走进一个地方）；句意是学生们依次进入考场。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -ance 后缀构成，义为「入口；进入」
同根变体名词，义为「进入；条目；参赛作品」
同根加前缀的名词，义为「娱乐；款待」

senses.title: To go or come into a place
senses.definition: to move from outside into a room, building or area
senses.definitionCN: 从外面走进房间、建筑或某个区域
senses.example: Please knock before you enter the office.
senses.exampleCN: 进办公室前请先敲门。
senses.why: The Latin root means to step across, so the image is one foot crossing the threshold.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语词根意为「跨步」，画面是一只脚跨过门槛。

senses.title: To take part in or join
senses.definition: to become a participant in a competition, exam or organization
senses.definitionCN: 成为比赛、考试或组织的参与者
senses.example: She decided to enter the speech contest.
senses.exampleCN: 她决定参加演讲比赛。
senses.why: Joining a contest is stepping into a field of players, an extension of crossing into a space.
senses.whyCN: 参加比赛就像走进选手的场地，是「跨入空间」意象的延伸。

senses.title: To put information into a system
senses.definition: to record information in a book, list or computer system
senses.definitionCN: 把信息记录在册、清单或电脑系统中
senses.example: Enter your password and press the button.
senses.exampleCN: 输入密码然后按下按钮。
senses.why: Data is made to go inside a machine, the same crossing image moved to paper and screens.
senses.whyCN: 数据被送进机器，同样的跨入画面移动到纸张与屏幕上。

senses.title: To become a member of a group or stage
senses.definition: to begin to belong to a profession, school or period of life
senses.definitionCN: 开始属于某个职业、学校或人生阶段
senses.example: He entered politics at a young age.
senses.exampleCN: 他很年轻就步入政界。
senses.why: A new stage of life is a new room, so joining it reuses the doorway picture.
senses.whyCN: 人生新阶段是一间新房间，加入它就复用门廊的画面。

intro.en: Enter comes from Old French entrer, from Latin intrare, built on intra meaning 'inside'. The core has always been crossing a line into a space.
intro.cn: enter 经古法语 entrer，来自拉丁语 intrare，词基 intra 意为「在内」。核心始终是跨过界线进入空间。

items.en: Latin intra meant 'inside, within', the root idea of the whole family.
items.cn: 拉丁语 intra 意为「在内、在内侧」，是整个词族的根意。

items.en: The verb intrare meant 'to go into, to enter', used of walking in as well as beginning something.
items.cn: 动词 intrare 意为「走进、进入」，既指走进，也指开始某事。

items.en: Old French entrer carried the verb into medieval European speech, still meaning to go in.
items.cn: 古法语 entrer 把动词带进中世纪欧洲语言，仍指进入。

items.en: English borrowed enter in the fourteenth century for both physical entry and joining activities.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入 enter，兼指实际进入与参加活动。

items.en: Computing added the data sense and the Enter key, extending the crossing image to screens.
items.cn: 计算领域增加了输入数据义与回车键，把跨入画面延伸到屏幕上。

note.en: The first group collects the same Latin intra family; the second collects near meanings about going in or joining.
note.cn: 第一组收集同一拉丁词 intra 的词族；第二组收集与「进入、参加」相关的近义词。

entries.definition: the door or gate by which one enters, or the act of entering
entries.definitionCN: 入口；进入。由 enter 加 -ance 构成。

entries.definition: the act of entering, an item in a list, or a contest submission
entries.definitionCN: 进入；条目；参赛作品。与 enter 同根的变体名词。

entries.definition: whole, unbroken; from the same Latin idea of what is held inside
entries.definitionCN: 完整的；同源于「包含在内」的拉丁语概念，词义已偏移。

entries.definition: to become a member of a group or activity
entries.definitionCN: 加入；参加。强调成为一员。

entries.definition: to enter a computer system with credentials
entries.definitionCN: 登录。特指进入计算机系统。

entries.definition: to go to a place or event regularly
entries.definitionCN: 出席；参加。强调到场或持续参与。

normalIntro.en: Five concrete hooks built from the real root and daily keyboard use.
normalIntro.cn: 五条基于真实词根与键盘日常的具体联想。

normal.en: ent- from Latin intra means inside: stepping in is entering.
normal.cn: ent-（在内，拉丁 intra）+ er：跨步进去，就是进入。

normal.en: The Enter key on the keyboard enters a new line every time.
normal.cn: 键盘上的 Enter 回车键：每按一次都在「进入」新一行。

normal.en: Pair entrance and enter as noun and verb.
normal.cn: entrance 入口 / enter 进入，名词与动词成对记。

normal.en: Enter the contest joins; enter data types, one virtual one real.
normal.cn: enter the contest 参加比赛；enter data 输入数据，一虚一实。

normal.en: The sound hints at granted special passage, for spelling only.
normal.cn: 谐音：「恩特」——恩准特别通道，大步进入，帮助拼读，不是词源。

abstract.en: Picture a shoe tip crossing a bright yellow threshold line.
abstract.cn: 画面：一只鞋尖跨过亮黄色门槛线的瞬间。

abstract.en: Push a glass door open and the world inside unfolds.
abstract.cn: 动作：伸手推开玻璃门，门内的世界豁然展开。

abstract.en: On the day you get into university, a new room of life opens.
abstract.cn: 感觉：考上大学那天，仿佛推开人生的新房间。

examples.en: You must enter the classroom before the bell rings.
examples.cn: 你必须在铃响前进入教室。

examples.en: More than one hundred students entered the contest.
examples.cn: 一百多名学生参加了这次比赛。

examples.en: Please enter your name at the top of the page.
examples.cn: 请把你的名字输入到页面顶端。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「恩特」——恩准特批，走进大门，谐音帮助拼读，不是词源。

root: enter 源自拉丁语 intra（在内），动词 intrare「走入」，经古法语 entrer 进入英语。同根词 entire、entrance、entry 都围绕「在内、跨入」的核心。

sensesIntro.en: Enter runs from stepping into a place, to joining an event, to feeding data inside a system, to entering a stage of life.
sensesIntro.cn: enter 从跨入空间，到参加活动，到输入数据，再到步入人生阶段，义项沿「跨入」不断延伸。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one foot crossing a threshold from outside to inside.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只脚从外面跨过门槛进入里面。

branches.cn: 进入房间、建筑与大门。
参加比赛、考试与组织。
输入姓名、数字与密码。
步入政界、大学或成年生活。
跨入任何新领域的共同第一步。

intro.en: Enter carries the Latin intra family clearly: inside, across, whole.
intro.cn: enter 清晰承载拉丁语 intra 词族：在内、跨过、完整。

latinIntro.en: Latin intra 'inside' is the shared ancestor of this group.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 intra「在内」是这一组的共同祖先。

items.example: Intravenous means within a vein.
Intrare gave Old French entrer.
items.exampleCN: intrare 衍生出古法语 entrer。

items.example: entrance names the act or place of entering.
items.exampleCN: entrance 指进入的动作或入口。

items.example: entry names one item entered in a list.
items.exampleCN: entry 指录入清单中的一条。

items.example: Interiors concern what is within borders.
Entire keeps the sense of what is held inside one boundary.
items.exampleCN: entire 保留「同一界限之内」的含义。

items.example: Entertain originally meant to keep someone within your care.
items.exampleCN: entertain 原义为把某人留在家中款待。

items.example: An entrance hall is the room you enter first.
items.exampleCN: 门厅是进入后首先到达的房间。

definition_zh: 环境；自然环境；周围状况；氛围
definition_en: the conditions, objects, and forces that surround a person, animal, or thing
core_image: 围在人身外的一圈：空气、水、人、规则都在圈里
scene: 森林样方里，研究员记录着温湿度等圈内的全部条件。The biologist recorded the temperature and humidity of the forest environment.
sceneCN: 这里 environment 是「（生物所处的）环境条件」（第 3 个义项：生物生活的周围条件）；句意：生物学家记录了森林环境的温度和湿度。图中可辨识物件：温湿度计、森林、记录本、树冠与苔藓。

derivatives.zh: 环境的；周围状况的
在环境方面；环保地
环境保护主义者
环境保护主义
（城镇的）周边地区；近郊

senses.title: The act of surrounding: what lies around
senses.definition: the conditions, objects, or forces that surround a person, animal, or thing
senses.definitionCN: 环绕着人、动物或事物的条件、物体或力量
senses.example: The laboratory environment must be kept free of dust.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室环境必须保持无尘。
senses.why: Environ came from Old French environer 'to surround', built on viron 'a circle'. Environment first named the state of being encircled, then the things doing the encircling.
senses.whyCN: environ 来自古法语 environer“环绕”，建立在 viron“圆圈”上。environment 最初指“被围住的状态”，随后指做包围的那些东西。

senses.title: The natural world: air, water, land, and life
senses.titleCN: 自然世界：空气、水、土地与生命
senses.definition: the natural world, especially as affected by human activity
senses.definitionCN: 自然世界，尤指受到人类活动影响时
senses.example: Plastic waste is one of the biggest threats to the environment.
senses.exampleCN: 塑料垃圾是对环境的最大威胁之一。
senses.why: From the 1950s ecology gave the surrounding circle a planetary meaning: the whole natural system that surrounds and supports life.
senses.whyCN: 20 世纪 50 年代起，生态学给了这个包围圈一层行星级含义：围绕并支撑生命的整个自然系统。

senses.title: Living conditions: where an organism lives
senses.titleCN: 生存条件：生物生活的地方
senses.definition: the conditions in which a person, animal, or plant lives or operates
senses.definitionCN: 人、动物或植物生活或运作所处的条件
senses.example: Cacti grow well in a dry environment.
senses.exampleCN: 仙人掌在干燥环境中长得好。
senses.why: For a living thing, the circle that surrounds it is made of climate, food, and shelter; the general surround narrows to a habitat.
senses.whyCN: 对生物来说，围住它的那个圈由气候、食物和庇护所构成；泛泛的“周围”缩小成了栖息环境。

senses.title: Social and cultural surroundings
senses.definition: the social, cultural, or economic conditions that shape behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 塑造行为的社会、文化或经济条件
senses.example: Children raised in a bilingual environment switch languages easily.
senses.exampleCN: 在双语环境中长大的孩子切换语言很轻松。
senses.why: People are surrounded by customs as much as by air. The circle becomes social, so environment names the culture that shapes a person.
senses.whyCN: 人既被空气包围，也被习俗包围。这个圈变成社会的，于是 environment 指塑造一个人的文化。

senses.title: Learning environment: conditions for study
senses.definition: in education, the physical and social conditions in which learning takes place
senses.definitionCN: 教育中指学习发生的物理与社会条件
senses.example: A quiet environment helps students concentrate.
senses.exampleCN: 安静的环境有助于学生集中注意力。
senses.why: Classrooms are a designed circle: lighting, noise, and relationships together set what a learner can do.
senses.whyCN: 教室是一个被设计出来的圈：灯光、噪音和人际关系共同决定学习者能做什么。

senses.title: Computing environment: the system a program runs in
senses.titleCN: 计算环境：程序运行所在的系统
senses.definition: in computing, the hardware and software conditions in which a program runs
senses.definitionCN: 计算机领域指程序运行所依赖的硬件与软件条件
senses.example: The old software will not run in a 64-bit environment.
senses.exampleCN: 这个旧软件无法在 64 位环境中运行。
senses.why: A program is surrounded by an operating system and settings; computing simply names that technical circle with the same word.
senses.whyCN: 程序被操作系统和各项设置包围；计算机领域只是用同一个词命名这个技术性的圈。

senses.title: The environment as a policy object
senses.definition: the environment, with the definite article, as the target of protection and regulation
senses.definitionCN: 带定冠词时，指保护与监管的对象
senses.example: The agency was created to protect the environment.
senses.exampleCN: 这个机构是为了保护环境而设立的。
senses.why: Once the natural circle is threatened, it becomes a thing to defend; the definite article marks the shared surroundings of all people.
senses.whyCN: 一旦自然之圈受到威胁，它就变成要捍卫的对象；定冠词标记的是所有人共享的周围世界。

senses.title: Business or market environment
senses.definition: the conditions under which a company or market operates
senses.definitionCN: 公司或市场运作所处的条件
senses.example: Low interest rates created a favourable environment for startups.
senses.exampleCN: 低利率为初创企业创造了有利的环境。
senses.why: Firms are surrounded by prices, rules, and rivals. The same circle, drawn around a market, gives the business sense.
senses.whyCN: 公司被价格、规则和对手包围。把同一个圈画在市场周围，就得到商业义。

senses.title: Environment vs surroundings: the whole set, not the items
senses.titleCN: environment 与 surroundings：整体条件，而非物件清单
senses.definition: the total set of conditions, as opposed to surroundings, which stresses the nearby objects
senses.definitionCN: 条件的整体集合，与强调附近物件的 surroundings 相对
senses.example: The patient's whole environment, not just the ward, affected recovery.
senses.exampleCN: 影响病人康复的是他的整个环境，而不只是病房。
senses.why: Environment names the enclosing system as a whole; surroundings counts the things nearby. The -ment ending marks the state of being surrounded, not a list of objects.
senses.whyCN: environment 命名整个包围系统；surroundings 数的是附近的物件。-ment 词尾标记“被包围的状态”，而不是一份物件清单。

intro.en: Environment began around 1600 as 'the state of being surrounded'. It grew from the verb environ 'to surround', and only in the 19th and 20th centuries did it become the word for natural and social conditions.
intro.cn: environment 约 1600 年以“被环绕的状态”出现。它由动词 environ“环绕”生长而来，直到 19、20 世纪才成为表示自然与社会条件的词。

items.en: First recorded meaning 'state of being environed', a noun of state built on the verb environ plus -ment.
items.cn: 最早记录义为“被环绕的状态”，是由动词 environ 加 -ment 构成的状态名词。

items.en: The verb environ 'to surround, encircle' is recorded in late 14th-century English.
items.cn: 动词 environ“环绕、围住”记录于 14 世纪晚期的英语。

items.en: From Old French environer, from environ 'around' = en- 'in' + viron 'circle, circuit', from virer 'to turn'.
items.cn: 来自古法语 environer，源自 environ“周围”= en-“内”+ viron“圆圈、一圈”，后者来自 virer“转”。

items.en: The sense 'the conditions in which a person or thing lives' is recorded in 1827, when Carlyle used it to translate German Umgebung.
items.cn: “人或物所处条件的总和”这一义项记录于 1827 年，卡莱尔用它翻译德语 Umgebung。

items.en: Ecology gives 'the natural world' its modern currency from 1956, and the environmental movement spreads it further.
items.cn: 生态学从 1956 年起让“自然世界”义流行起来，环保运动又把它传播得更广。

items.en: Modern English extends environment to computing and business; the old verb survives mainly in the plural noun environs, 'the outskirts'.
items.cn: 现代英语把 environment 扩展到计算机与商业领域；旧动词主要保留在复数名词 environs“近郊”中。

note.en: The first group is chosen for spelling and sound, the second for meaning, so that form and sense stay separate.
note.cn: 第一组按拼写和读音挑选，第二组按词义挑选，这样词形和词义不会混在一起。

entries.definition: the area around a town or place. It names the outskirts, not the total conditions.
entries.definitionCN: 城镇周边的地区；近郊。它指外围地带，而不是条件的总和。

entries.definition: relating to the environment. It is the adjective formed from the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 环境的；与环境有关的。它是由该名词构成的形容词。

entries.definition: to surround, a rare formal verb. Environment is the noun built from it with -ment.
entries.definitionCN: 环绕；围住，是罕用的正式动词。environment 是它加 -ment 构成的名词。

entries.definition: the things and conditions near someone. It counts nearby objects, while environment names the whole system.
entries.definitionCN: 周围的事物与条件。它数的是附近物件，而 environment 指整个系统。

entries.definition: the place or background where something happens. It is narrower and often used of stories or scenes.
entries.definitionCN: 某事发生的地点或背景。它更窄，常用于故事或场景。

entries.definition: the natural home of a plant or animal. It is a biologist's term for one species' environment.
entries.definitionCN: 动植物的天然栖息地。它是生物学术语，指某一物种的环境。

entries.definition: the social and cultural background of a person or group. It is literary and almost always social.
entries.definitionCN: 个人或群体的社会文化背景。它偏文学，几乎总指社会层面。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: environ plus -ment, the viron 'circle' inside the word, and the surviving relatives environ, environs and environmental.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：environ + -ment、词内的 viron“圆圈”，以及仍活着的同族词 environ、environs、environmental。

normal.en: environ means 'to surround', and -ment turns the action into a state: environment is the state of being surrounded.
normal.cn: environ 意为“环绕”，-ment 把动作变成状态：environment 就是“被围住的状态”。

normal.en: viron meant 'circle, circuit' in Old French, and virer 'to turn' is the same source as English veer.
normal.cn: viron 在古法语中意为“圆圈、一圈”，而 virer“转”与英语 veer 同源。

normal.en: environs keeps the old verb alive: it means the area that circles a town.
normal.cn: environs 让旧动词继续活着：它指环绕城镇的那片外围地区。

normal.en: environmental, environmentally, environmentalist and environmentalism are the modern derivatives built on the noun.
normal.cn: environmental、environmentally、environmentalist、environmentalism 都是在这个名词上构成的现代派生词。

normal.en: the environment, with the definite article, is the shared natural circle that policy tries to protect.
normal.cn: 带定冠词的 the environment，是政策试图保护的那个共享自然之圈。

abstract.en: Draw a circle around a body: inside it put air, water, food, people and rules.
abstract.cn: 在一个身体周围画一个圈：圈里放空气、水、食物、人和规则。

abstract.en: The same circle can shrink to a classroom, a lab, or a server, and expand to the whole planet.
abstract.cn: 同一个圈可以缩小到一间教室、一间实验室或一台服务器，也可以扩大到整个星球。

abstract.en: What surrounds also shapes: the circle is not a backdrop but a set of forces acting on what lives inside.
abstract.cn: 包围者也在塑造：这个圈不是背景板，而是一组作用于圈内生命的力量。

examples.en: The desert environment is harsh for both plants and animals.
examples.cn: 沙漠环境对植物和动物都很严酷。

examples.en: She grew up in an environment where books were always available.
examples.cn: 她在书籍随手可及的环境中长大。

examples.en: The program stores its settings in an environment file.
examples.cn: 该程序把设置保存在一个环境文件里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因围门」——因为四周都围上了门，圈出一块地方 → environment 环境、周围状况

root: 源自古法语 environ“环绕”= en-“内”+ viron“圆圈”← virer“转”，核心是“围在人或物外面的一圈条件”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of environment all come from one circle drawn around a person, animal, or thing. The circle can shrink to a room or a server, or expand to the whole natural world.
sensesIntro.cn: environment 的九个义项都来自画在人、动物或事物外面的同一个圈。这个圈可以缩小到一间房或一台服务器，也可以扩大到整个自然世界。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a circle drawn around a body, holding air, water, people and rules.
core.cn: 核心意象：围绕一个身体画出的圈，圈里装着空气、水、人与规则。

branches.en: THE CIRCLE ITSELF: the state of being surrounded, and the total set of conditions around a body.
branches.cn: 圈本身：被包围的状态，以及相对于附近物件清单的整体条件。

branches.en: NATURE AND HABITAT: the planetary natural system, and the narrower conditions in which one organism lives.
branches.cn: 自然与栖息地：行星级的自然系统，以及某一生物生活的较窄条件。

branches.en: PEOPLE AND LEARNING: social and cultural surroundings where people grow and learn.
branches.cn: 人与学习：社会文化氛围，以及教室这类被设计的学习条件。

branches.en: TECHNICAL AND MARKET CIRCLES: the system that a program, machine or business operates within.
branches.cn: 技术与市场之圈：程序周围的系统，以及公司周围的条件。

branches.en: POLICY: the shared natural circle that governments promise to protect.
branches.cn: 政策：共享的自然之圈变成国家保护的对象。

intro.en: Environment is en- plus viron 'circle' plus -ment, a noun of state. English builds environmental, environmentally, environmentalist and environmentalism on top, and keeps the bare verb environ.
intro.cn: environment 是 en- + viron“圆圈”+ -ment 构成的状态名词。英语在其上构成 environmental、environmentally、environmentalist、environmentalism，并保留光秃的动词 environ。

latinIntro.en: There is no reliable Latin ancestor to list. The word comes from Old French environer, and the deeper origin of viron and virer is uncertain, with only a possible link to Latin vibrare 'to shake'.
latinIntro.cn: 没有可靠的拉丁祖先可列。这个词来自古法语 environer，viron 与 virer 的更深来源不确定，只有与拉丁语 vibrare“摇动”的可能联系。

items.meaning: the state of being surrounded; the surrounding conditions
items.meaningCN: 被环绕的状态；周围条件（-ment 构成状态名词）
items.example: A calm environment helps children learn.
items.exampleCN: 平静的环境有助于孩子学习。

items.meaningCN: 环绕；围住（罕用的正式动词）
items.example: Tall hedges environ the old garden.
items.exampleCN: 高高的树篱环绕着这座老花园。

items.meaningCN: 周边地区；近郊（-s 构成复数名词）
items.example: Many commuters live in the environs of the city.
items.exampleCN: 许多通勤者住在城市近郊。

items.meaningCN: 环境的（-al 构成形容词）
items.example: The report lists the main environmental risks.
items.exampleCN: 报告列出了主要的环境风险。

items.meaningCN: 在环境方面；环保地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The building is environmentally friendly.

items.meaning: a person who works to protect the environment
items.meaningCN: 环境保护主义者（-ist 表示人）
items.example: The environmentalist opposed the new road.
items.exampleCN: 那位环保人士反对修建新公路。

items.meaning: the movement to protect the natural world
items.meaningCN: 环境保护主义（-ism 表示主义、运动）
items.example: Environmentalism grew quickly in the 1970s.
items.exampleCN: 环境保护主义在 20 世纪 70 年代迅速发展。

items.meaningCN: 突然转向（与 virer“转”同源）
items.example: The boat veered away from the rocks.
items.exampleCN: 小船突然转向，避开了礁石。

definition_zh: 自然环境的；生态环境的；周围环境的；环境因素的；环境保护的；环境艺术的
definition_en: relating to the natural world and its condition; relating to a person's or organism's surroundings and conditions; concerned with protecting nature; (biology) arising from external conditions rather than genes; (art) concerned with the experience of a space
core_image: 一圈看不见的膜把人和周围的一切隔开又连上：你呼吸的空气、踩的地、听见的噪声都在这一圈里
scene: 工厂代表指着监测屏上的水质曲线。The plant manager points at the water-quality curve and says the report assesses the environmental impact of the project.
sceneCN: 这里 environmental 是「环境的、环境影响的」（第 1 个义项：与自然环境及其状况相关）；句意：代表指着水质曲线说，这份报告评估项目的环境影响。图中可辨识物件：监测屏、水质曲线、取样瓶、工厂厂区。

pos.zh: 自然环境的；生态环境的；环境保护的（常与 impact / protection / law 连用）
周围环境的；由环境引起的；（艺术）环境艺术的（较专业用法）

derivatives.zh: 环境；周围状况
在环境方面；环保地
环境保护主义
环保主义者；环保的

senses.title: Relating to the natural world
senses.definition: relating to the natural world, especially its air, water, land, and living systems
senses.definitionCN: 与自然世界相关，尤指空气、水、土地与生命系统
senses.example: The project underwent a full environmental review before construction.
senses.exampleCN: 项目在施工前接受了全面的环境审查。
senses.why: Environmental is environment + -al. Environment is environ + -ment, where environ 'to surround' comes from Old French environ 'around'. The adjective therefore begins with the image of everything that surrounds a living thing.
senses.whyCN: environmental 是 environment + -al。environment 是 environ + -ment，其中 environ“包围”来自古法语 environ“在周围”。因此这个形容词的起点是“包围着生命体的一切”这一意象。

senses.title: Relating to surroundings or conditions
senses.definition: relating to the conditions, objects, and influences that surround a person, organism, or activity
senses.definitionCN: 与包围着人、生物或活动的条件、物体与影响相关
senses.example: Temperature and light are key environmental variables in the experiment.
senses.exampleCN: 温度与光照是实验中的关键环境变量。
senses.why: This is the broader, non-green sense: environment can be a laboratory room or a social setting. The adjective simply says 'of the surroundings', and context decides which surroundings count.
senses.whyCN: 这是更宽、非“环保”的义项：environment 可以是实验室房间或社会环境。形容词只说“周围状况的”，至于算哪些周围，由语境决定。

senses.title: Concerned with protecting nature
senses.definition: relating to efforts, laws, or groups that aim to protect nature from harm
senses.definitionCN: 与旨在保护自然免受损害的努力、法律或团体相关
senses.example: Environmental groups challenged the permit in court.
senses.exampleCN: 环保团体在法庭上质疑该许可。
senses.why: By metonymy the word shifts from 'of the environment' to 'protecting the environment'. This is the dominant everyday sense in news and policy, and it carries an implicit stance rather than a neutral description.
senses.whyCN: 通过转喻，这个词从“环境的”转到“保护环境的”。这是新闻与政策中最主要的日常义，它带有隐含立场，而非中性描述。

senses.title: Relating to environmental health
senses.definition: relating to conditions that affect public health, such as air quality, water safety, and waste
senses.definitionCN: 与影响公共卫生的状况相关，如空气质量、饮水安全与废物
senses.example: The agency investigates environmental health risks in old housing.
senses.exampleCN: 该机构调查老旧住房中的环境卫生风险。
senses.why: Public health uses the adjective to connect illness to place: lead paint, bad air, and contaminated water are environmental exposures. Here nature and human health are measured together.
senses.whyCN: 公共卫生用这个形容词把疾病与地点连起来：含铅涂料、劣质空气与受污染的水都是环境暴露。这里自然与人类健康被一起衡量。

senses.title: Arising from external conditions in biology
senses.titleCN: 生物学中由外部条件引起的
senses.definition: caused by external conditions rather than by genetic inheritance
senses.definitionCN: 由外部条件而非遗传引起
senses.example: The study separated genetic from environmental causes of the disease.
senses.exampleCN: 该研究把这种病的遗传成因与环境成因分开。
senses.why: Biology uses the term in the nature–nurture contrast: environmental effects are everything the genome does not supply. The adjective marks a cause, not a setting, which is why it pairs with 'factors' and 'influences'.
senses.whyCN: 生物学在“先天—后天”对照中使用这个术语：环境效应是基因组未提供的一切。这个形容词标记的是原因，而非场景，所以常与 factors、influences 搭配。

senses.title: Relating to environmental art
senses.definition: relating to art that treats a place, space, or landscape as part of the work
senses.definitionCN: 与把地点、空间或景观作为作品一部分的艺术相关
senses.example: The environmental installation changed how visitors moved through the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 这件环境装置改变了观众在大厅中移动的方式。
senses.why: Art criticism uses 'environmental' for works that surround the viewer rather than hang in front of them. This sense is unrelated to ecology; the shared word is 'surroundings'.
senses.whyCN: 艺术批评用 environmental 指包围观众、而非挂在观众面前的作品。这个义项与生态无关，共享的词义是“周围”。

senses.title: Subject to environmental regulation
senses.definition: governed by rules on pollution, land use, or ecological impact
senses.definitionCN: 受污染、土地使用或生态影响方面的规则约束
senses.example: The plant needs an environmental permit to discharge treated water.
senses.exampleCN: 该厂需要环境许可才能排放处理过的水。
senses.why: Legal usage nominalizes the word into fixed phrases: environmental law, environmental impact assessment, environmental permit. Here the adjective marks a regulatory domain with defined procedures.
senses.whyCN: 法律用法把这个词名物化为固定短语：environmental law、environmental impact assessment、environmental permit。这里形容词标记一个有既定程序的监管领域。

senses.title: Environmentally oriented in design
senses.definition: designed or operated with low harm to the environment in mind
senses.definitionCN: 在设计或运行上以低环境损害为取向
senses.example: The building's environmental features include grey-water reuse and passive cooling.
senses.exampleCN: 这栋建筑的环境友好特性包括中水回用与被动降温。
senses.why: Engineering extends the word to products and buildings: environmental design is design that accounts for resources and emissions. It overlaps with 'green' and 'sustainable' but is more technical and less promotional.
senses.whyCN: 工程学把词扩展到产品与建筑：environmental design 是考虑资源与排放的设计。它与 green、sustainable 重叠，但更技术化、更少宣传色彩。

intro.en: Environmental is environment + -al. Environment is a French-derived noun: environ 'to surround' + -ment. Environ comes from Old French environ 'around', built on viron 'circuit', whose further origin is uncertain. English environmental is a nineteenth-century adjective, and its 'green' sense is largely a twentieth-century development.
intro.cn: environmental 是 environment + -al。environment 是法语来源名词：environ“包围”+ -ment。environ 来自古法语 environ“在周围”，建立在 viron“环、圈”上，更早来源不确定。英语 environmental 是 19 世纪形容词，其“环保”义主要是 20 世纪的发展。

items.en: Old French environ meant 'around, in a circle', from en- 'in' plus viron 'circuit, circle'. The verb environner 'to surround' and the noun environnement developed from it.
items.cn: 古法语 environ 意为“在周围、成圈”，由 en-“在内”加 viron“环、圈”构成。动词 environner“包围”与名词 environnement 由此发展。

items.en: The origin of viron 'circle' is uncertain. It may be linked to virer 'to turn', but the further etymology of virer is itself disputed; no reliable Latin source can be asserted.
items.cn: viron“环、圈”的来源不确定。它可能与 virer“转动”有关，但 virer 的更早词源本身有争议；无法断言可靠的拉丁来源。

items.en: English borrowed environment in the seventeenth century as 'the act of surrounding' and 'surrounding conditions'. The modern sense of natural surroundings consolidated in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries.
items.cn: 英语于 17 世纪借入 environment，义为“包围的行为”与“周围状况”。自然环境的现代义在 18、19 世纪逐步定型。

items.en: Environmental appears as the adjective of environment in the nineteenth century. Early uses concern surroundings and conditions generally, not pollution or ecology.
items.cn: environmental 于 19 世纪作为 environment 的形容词出现。早期用法泛指周围与条件，而非污染或生态。

items.en: With the rise of ecology and the environmental movement after the mid-twentieth century, the adjective shifted toward nature protection: environmental law, environmental impact, environmental groups.
items.cn: 20 世纪中叶以后，随着生态学与环保运动的兴起，这个形容词转向自然保护：environmental law、environmental impact、environmental groups。

items.en: The word now spans laboratory variables, public health, art installations, and building design. The unifying idea is still 'what surrounds', which is why one adjective can serve ecology and aesthetics at once.
items.cn: 这个词如今覆盖实验室变量、公共卫生、艺术装置与建筑设计。统一的概念仍是“包围着什么”，所以一个形容词能同时服务生态与美学。

note.en: The first group separates the environment family from look-alikes; the second group separates environmental from neighbouring adjectives of nature and surroundings.
note.cn: 第一组区分 environment 词族与形近词；第二组区分 environmental 与相邻的“自然”“周围”形容词。

entries.definition: the surroundings or conditions in which something exists. It is the noun that -al turns into the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 某物存在的周围状况或条件。它是被 -al 转化为形容词的名词。

entries.definition: in a way that relates to or affects the environment, as in environmentally friendly. It modifies an adjective or verb, not a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 以与环境相关或影响环境的方式，如 environmentally friendly。它修饰形容词或动词，而非名词。

entries.definition: to surround or encircle. It is the oldest member of the family and now rare outside 'environment'.
entries.definitionCN: 包围、环绕。它是词族中最古老的成员，如今除 environment 外很少见。

entries.definition: relating to ecology, the study of organisms and their interactions. It is more technical than environmental and not necessarily about protection.
entries.definitionCN: 与生态学相关，即研究生物及其互动。它比 environmental 更技术化，也不一定涉及保护。

entries.definition: existing or happening around something. It is neutral and spatial, while environmental can imply conditions or regulation.
entries.definitionCN: 存在于或发生在某物周围的。它中性且空间化，而 environmental 可暗示条件或法规。

entries.definition: environmentally friendly, often used in marketing. It is looser and more promotional than environmental.
entries.definitionCN: 环保的，常用于营销。它比 environmental 更松、更带宣传色彩。

normalIntro.en: Real associations: environ 'to surround', the -ment noun, the -al adjective, and fixed phrases such as environmental impact and environmental law.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联想：environ“包围”、-ment 名词、-al 形容词，以及 environmental impact、environmental law 等固定短语。

normal.en: environ means 'to surround': environment is everything that surrounds us, and -al makes it the adjective.
normal.cn: environ 意为“包围”：environment 是包围我们的一切，-al 使它成为形容词。

normal.en: environment + -al: keep the -ment and add -al; the adverb then adds -ly.
normal.cn: environment + -al：保留 -ment 再加 -al；副词再加 -ly。

normal.en: Environmental impact, environmental law, environmental protection: the three phrases cover most news uses.
normal.cn: environmental impact、environmental law、environmental protection：这三个短语覆盖了大部分新闻用法。

normal.en: In biology, environmental means 'caused from outside', the opposite of genetic.
normal.cn: 生物学中 environmental 意为“由外部引起的”，与 genetic 相对。

normal.en: Environmental art surrounds the viewer; it borrows the word's oldest sense of 'surroundings', not its green sense.
normal.cn: 环境艺术包围观众；它借的是这个词最古老的“周围”义，而非环保义。

abstract.en: An environment is not a backdrop but a set of conditions that enter the body with every breath.
abstract.cn: 环境不是背景板，而是一套随每次呼吸进入身体的条件。

abstract.en: To call something environmental is to admit that its causes and effects cross its own boundary.
abstract.cn: 把某事称为 environmental，就是承认它的因果越过了自身边界。

abstract.en: Protection and surroundings share one word because what surrounds us is also what we must defend.
abstract.cn: 保护与周围共享一个词，因为包围我们的事物也是我们必须守护的事物。

examples.en: The environmental impact of the dam was assessed over three years.
examples.cn: 大坝的环境影响经过三年评估。

examples.en: Environmental factors explain part of the difference in height between the groups.
examples.cn: 环境因素解释了各组身高差异的一部分。

examples.en: The city adopted stricter environmental rules on waste water.
examples.cn: 该市对废水采取了更严格的环境规定。

dict_mnemonic.text: “因外绕，门头”——因为外面绕着一圈东西，门口就成了环境 → environmental 环境的

root: environ（包围，古法语 environ“在周围”）+ -ment（名词后缀）+ -al（形容词后缀）；字面义“包围着（我们）的”，核心是“与周围状况或自然世界相关”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of environmental spread outward from one idea: what surrounds a thing. That surrounding can be nature, a laboratory, a body, a genome's absence, a gallery space, a legal regime, or a building's design. The 'green' sense is the most visible today but not the oldest.
sensesIntro.cn: environmental 的八个义项都从一个观念向外展开：包围某物的一切。这个“周围”可以是自然、实验室、身体、基因之外的因素、画廊空间、法律体制或建筑设计。“环保”义今天最显眼，却不是最古老的。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an invisible membrane that both separates a living thing from its surroundings and connects it to them.
core.cn: 核心意象：一层看不见的膜，既把生命体与周围隔开，又把它与周围连在一起。

branches.en: WHAT SURROUNDS: the natural world and the laboratory's variables are both the set of conditions around a thing.
branches.cn: 包围之物：自然世界与实验室变量都是某物周围的条件集合。

branches.en: PROTECTION AND HEALTH: the adjective turns from describing surroundings to defending them, and to health effects that enter through them.
branches.cn: 保护与健康：形容词从描述周围转为守护周围，并指向通过周围进入健康的影响。

branches.en: CAUSE: in biology, environmental marks what the genome does not supply.
branches.cn: 原因：生物学中 environmental 标记基因组未提供的东西。

branches.en: ART: the work surrounds the viewer, using the oldest sense of the word.
branches.cn: 艺术：作品包围观众，用的是这个词最古老的义。

branches.en: REGULATION AND DESIGN: law defines the domain, and engineering builds products that lower their load on it.
branches.cn: 法规与设计：法律界定领域，工程建造降低环境负荷的产品。

intro.en: Environmental is a two-suffix adjective: environ + -ment + -al. The affix set shows the noun, adverb, and related forms, and warns that the root viron is of uncertain origin.
intro.cn: environmental 是双后缀形容词：environ + -ment + -al。词缀组展示名词、副词与相关形式，并提醒词根 viron 来源不确定。

latinIntro.en: Old French viron 'circle' and environ 'around' yield the verb environner and the noun environnement; English adds -al. No reliable Latin cognate for viron can be asserted, so the Latin entries are left empty rather than invented.
latinIntro.cn: 古法语 viron“圈”与 environ“在周围”产生动词 environner 与名词 environnement；英语再加 -al。无法断言 viron 有可靠拉丁同源词，因此拉丁条目留空，而不编造。

items.meaning: relating to surroundings or the natural world
items.meaningCN: 环境的；环保的（-al 构成形容词）
items.example: The environmental review took a year.

items.meaning: the conditions or surroundings of something
items.example: Children learn from their environment.

items.meaningCN: 在环境方面；环保地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The product is environmentally friendly.

items.meaning: a movement to protect the natural world
items.meaningCN: 环境保护主义（-ism 表主义）
items.example: Environmentalism grew rapidly in the 1970s.
items.exampleCN: 环保主义在 1970 年代迅速发展。

items.meaning: a person who works to protect nature
items.example: Environmentalists opposed the new road.
items.exampleCN: 环保主义者反对这条新路。

items.example: Trees environ the old house.
items.exampleCN: 树木环绕着这座老房子。

items.meaning: the effect of an activity on the surroundings
items.example: The environmental impact was rated low.

items.meaning: the body of rules protecting the natural world
items.example: Environmental law governs waste disposal.

definition_zh: 逃跑；逃脱；逃离；避开；泄漏；逃生
definition_en: to get away from a place, danger or someone's control
core_image: 冲出牢笼：从限制的包围中破口而出
scene: 动物园围栏的门没关好，一只小鸟扑翅而出。The bird escaped from its open cage at dusk.
sceneCN: 这里 escape 是「逃脱」（第 1 个义项：离开限制之地）；句意是小鸟在黄昏时逃出了敞开的笼子。

collocations.zh: 逃过某人的注意；被忽视

derivatives.zh: 同根加后缀构成的名词，义为「恶作剧；越轨行为」
由 escape 加 -ist 构成，义为「逃避现实的人」
由 escape 加 -ism 构成，义为「逃避主义；自我逃避」

senses.title: To get away from a place
senses.definition: to leave a place where you are kept, or to get out of danger
senses.definitionCN: 离开被关押的地方，或脱离危险
senses.example: The prisoners escaped through a hidden tunnel.
senses.exampleCN: 囚犯们通过一条隐蔽的地道逃走了。
senses.why: The root idea is slipping out of a restraining cloak, so the image is breaking out of an enclosure.
senses.whyCN: 词根本义是从束缚的斗篷中滑出，画面是冲出围困之处。

senses.title: To avoid something unpleasant
senses.definition: to succeed in avoiding something harmful or unwanted
senses.definitionCN: 成功躲开有害或不想遭遇的事
senses.example: The town escaped the worst of the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 这座小镇躲过了风暴最猛烈的袭击。
senses.why: Dangers chase you like keepers chase a prisoner, so dodging them is another way of not being caught.
senses.whyCN: 危险如看守追捕逃犯，躲开它们即另一种「未被抓住」。

senses.title: To leak or get out of a container
senses.definition: of gas, liquid or information, to get out of where it should be held
senses.definitionCN: 气体、液体或信息从本应被容纳之处跑出来
senses.example: Gas was escaping from the broken pipe.
senses.exampleCN: 煤气正从破裂的管道中逸出。
senses.why: What is confined longs to be out, so the same breaking-out image applies to steam and secrets.
senses.whyCN: 被约束之物渴望外出，同样的破围画面也适用于蒸汽与秘密。

senses.title: An act of getting away
senses.definition: the act or way of getting away, or something that frees the mind from daily life
senses.definitionCN: 逃脱的行为或方式，也指让心灵摆脱日常的事
senses.example: Reading is her escape from a busy day.
senses.exampleCN: 读书是她从忙碌一天中解脱的方式。
senses.why: Once the verb is settled, the noun names the break itself, both physical and mental.
senses.whyCN: 动词定型后，名词指那次突破本身，既指身体也指心灵。

intro.en: Escape comes from Vulgar Latin and Old French words about slipping out of a cloak. The picture of getting out of a covering has stayed with the word for a thousand years.
intro.cn: escape 经通俗拉丁语与古法语，本义为「从斗篷中滑脱」。脱出覆盖物的画面伴随这个词上千年。

items.en: Vulgar Latin excappare meant 'to slip out of one's cape', from ex- (out) and cappa (cloak).
items.cn: 通俗拉丁语 excappare 意为「脱出斗篷」，由 ex-（向外）与 cappa（斗篷）构成。

items.en: Old French eschaper kept the meaning 'to get free, to slip away', the cloak still implied.
items.cn: 古法语 eschaper 沿用「脱身、溜走」之意，斗篷意象仍在。

items.en: English borrowed the word in the thirteenth century as escapen, first about prisoners and captives.
items.cn: 英语在十三世纪借入 escapen，最早用于囚犯与被俘者。

items.en: By the seventeenth century the word covered leaking gas and avoiding danger, extending the breakout image.
items.cn: 到十七世纪，词义扩展到气体泄漏与躲避危险，破围意象延伸。

items.en: The mental sense, an escape from daily life, became common in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 「逃离日常」的心理意义在十九世纪变得常用。

note.en: The first group collects the same cloak-root family; the second collects near meanings about getting away.
note.cn: 第一组收集同一「斗篷」词根的词族；第二组收集与「逃离」相关的近义词。

entries.definition: a wild or reckless act of breaking rules
entries.definitionCN: 恶作剧；越轨行为。同根词，指突破规矩的举动。

entries.definition: the habit of avoiding unpleasant reality through fantasy or fun
entries.definitionCN: 逃避主义。由 escape 加 -ism 构成。

entries.definition: a sleeveless cloak; the very garment in the original image
entries.definitionCN: 斗篷；披肩。正是词源画面中的那件衣服。

entries.definition: to run away quickly, often from serious danger
entries.definitionCN: 逃走；逃离。强调急速离开，多用于重大危险。

entries.definition: to avoid cleverly, often duties or questions
entries.definitionCN: 回避；逃避。强调巧妙躲开责任或提问。

entries.definition: to escape suddenly from prison or confinement
entries.definitionCN: 突然逃脱；爆发。多指集体越狱或冲突爆发。

normalIntro.en: Five concrete hooks built from the real cloak root and daily phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 五条基于「斗篷」词根与日常搭配的具体联想。

normal.en: es- means out and cape means cloak: sliding out of the cloak is escaping.
normal.cn: es-（出）+ cape（斗篷）：从斗篷里滑出去，就是逃脱。

normal.en: Cape still names a real cloak today, so the root picture is touchable.
normal.cn: cape 一词至今仍是斗篷，词源画面可见可触。

normal.en: A narrow escape means you almost did not get away.
normal.cn: narrow escape 死里逃生，差点没逃掉，反义衬托。

normal.en: The fire escape is the route out when fire blocks the stairs.
normal.cn: fire escape 太平梯：火灾时的逃生路线。

normal.en: The sound hints at lifting a cover and running, for spelling only.
normal.cn: 谐音：「一斯盖就跑」——掀开覆盖物就跑，帮助拼读，不是词源。

abstract.en: Picture a bird pushing out of a half-open cage at dusk.
abstract.cn: 画面：黄昏时小鸟扑出半开的鸟笼。

abstract.en: Feel the cold air rush in as you slip out of a heavy cloak.
abstract.cn: 动作：从厚重斗篷滑出时冷风灌入的瞬间。

abstract.en: Imagine steam hissing out of a cracked pipe, small but unstoppable.
abstract.cn: 感觉：蒸汽从裂缝嘶嘶逸出，微小却不可阻挡。

examples.en: Two lions escaped from the zoo last night.
examples.cn: 昨晚两只狮子从动物园逃走了。

examples.en: We had a narrow escape on the icy road.
examples.cn: 我们在结冰的路上死里逃生。

examples.en: Some heat escaped from the broken window.
examples.cn: 一些热量从破窗中散失了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一斯盖」——一掀开盖子就跑，谐音帮助拼读，不是词源。

root: escape 源自通俗拉丁语 excappare（ex- 向外 + cappa 斗篷），经古法语 eschaper 进入英语，本义为「脱出斗篷」，核心是挣脱覆盖与束缚。

sensesIntro.en: Escape runs from breaking out of a place, to dodging danger, to leaking out, to the mental break from daily life.
sensesIntro.cn: escape 从冲出某地，到躲开危险，到气体逸出，再到心灵逃离日常，义项沿「脱出」延伸。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: slipping out of a covering or enclosure.
core.cn: 核心意象：从覆盖物或围困中滑脱而出。

branches.cn: 囚犯、动物与人离开被禁之地。
小镇躲过风暴、人们躲开责难。
煤气、水与秘密悄悄溜出。
以读书或旅行逃离日常。
不再被束缚的共同状态。

intro.en: Escape carries the Latin ex- out-prefix and the cappa cloak root visibly.
intro.cn: escape 清晰保留拉丁 ex-「向外」前缀与 cappa「斗篷」词根。

latinIntro.en: Vulgar Latin excappare is the shared ancestor; the cloak family is small but real.
latinIntro.cn: 通俗拉丁语 excappare 是共同祖先；斗篷词族不大但真实。

items.example: Escape means getting out.
A cape is still worn today.
An escapade is a playful breakout.
Escapism is the habit of escaping reality.
items.exampleCN: escapism 指逃避现实的习性。

items.example: An escapist escapes into fantasy.
Export means to carry out.
Capture is the opposite of escape.
items.exampleCN: capture 恰是 escape 的反面。

items.example: Buildings mark the fire escape clearly.

latinEntries.meaning: to slip out of a cape

definition_zh: 尤其；特别；格外；主要地
definition_en: more than usual, or more than other things; particularly
core_image: 聚光灯：在一群东西中把一束光打到某个上
scene: 满桌家常菜里，那盘糖醋排骨最先被夹空。I love this restaurant, especially its sweet and sour ribs.
sceneCN: 这里 especially 是「尤其」（第 1 个义项：突出其中之一）；句意是我爱这家店，尤其爱糖醋排骨。

derivatives.zh: 去掉后缀的基础形容词，义为「特别的；专门的」
由 special 加 -ty 构成，义为「专业；特产；招牌菜」
由 special 加 -ist 构成，义为「专家；专科医生」

senses.title: Particularly, more than others
senses.definition: used to single out one person or thing from a group as more notable
senses.definitionCN: 从一群中特别点出某人或某物
senses.example: Everyone was tired, especially the little boy.
senses.exampleCN: 大家都很累，尤其是那个小男孩。
senses.why: Special means set apart, and the -ly adverb points the setting-apart at one member of the group.
senses.whyCN: special 本义是「被单独挑出」，-ly 副词把这种「挑出」指向群体中的某一个。

senses.title: To a great degree
senses.definition: very much, or to an unusual extent, often before adjectives in informal use
senses.definitionCN: 程度很深，口语中常放在形容词前
senses.example: The soup was especially good that day.
senses.exampleCN: 那天这汤格外好喝。
senses.why: A singled-out thing is also lifted above the average, so the word slides into meaning very.
senses.whyCN: 被挑出之物也被抬到平均线之上，于是词义滑向「非常」。

senses.title: For a particular purpose or person
senses.definition: made or done for one special purpose or person
senses.definitionCN: 为特定目的或人而做
senses.example: This gift was bought especially for your birthday.
senses.exampleCN: 这份礼物是特意为你的生日买的。
senses.why: When something is set apart for one use, the direction of the setting-apart becomes purpose.
senses.whyCN: 当某物被单独留作一用时，「挑出」的方向就成了目的。

intro.en: Especially comes from special, which traces to Latin species meaning appearance or kind. To be special is to be set apart as its own kind.
intro.cn: especially 由 special 派生，special 上溯拉丁语 species「外形、种类」。special 即「被单独归为一类」。

items.en: Latin species meant 'appearance, look, kind', the visible form by which things are told apart.
items.cn: 拉丁语 species 意为「外形、样子、种类」，是区分事物的可见形式。

items.en: The adjective specialis meant 'of a particular kind, individual', built on the root of species.
items.cn: 形容词 specialis 意为「特定种类的、个体的」，建在 species 词根上。

items.en: Old French special kept the meaning 'particular, distinctive' in medieval use.
items.cn: 古法语 special 在中世纪沿用「特别的、有区别的」之意。

items.en: English took special in the thirteenth century and formed especially shortly after.
items.cn: 英语在十三世纪借入 special，随后不久造出 especially。

items.en: The adverb settled into its modern uses, from singling out to meaning very much.
items.cn: 副词定型为现代用法，从「特别指出」到「非常」。

note.en: The first group collects the same species family; the second collects near meanings about singling out.
note.cn: 第一组收集同一 species 词族的词；第二组收集与「特别指出」相关的近义词。

entries.definition: for one special purpose; often used of things made to order
entries.definitionCN: 特意地；专门地。与 especially 形近，侧重「专门为某目的」。

entries.definition: a kind of plant or animal; the Latin source word itself
entries.definitionCN: 物种；种类。正是拉丁语源头词。

entries.definition: a sample taken to show what a kind looks like
entries.definitionCN: 标本；样本。同根，指展示种类的样例。

entries.definition: especially; a close synonym in almost all uses
entries.definitionCN: 尤其；特别。几乎所有用法中的近义词。

entries.definition: for the most part; stresses the largest share
entries.definitionCN: 主要地。侧重占比最大。

entries.definition: in a way worth noticing; formal and written
entries.definitionCN: 显著地；尤其（正式）。多用于书面。

normalIntro.en: Five concrete hooks built from the real root and classroom sentences.
normalIntro.cn: 五条基于真实词根与课堂例句的具体联想。

normal.en: e plus special plus ly: special turned into an adverb of stress.
normal.cn: e + special + ly：special 加上 ly 就成了副词「尤其」。

normal.en: Species is the Latin source meaning kind; a special thing is its own kind.
normal.cn: species 是拉丁源头「种类」，被单挑一类即 special。

normal.en: Especially for you is the line every gift card uses.
normal.cn: especially for you 是礼物卡片上最常见的话。

normal.en: Especially in summer opens a common seasonal example.
normal.cn: especially in summer：季节举例常用开头。

normal.en: The sound hints at picking out one special item at a glance.
normal.cn: 谐音：「一斯佩挑」——一眼挑出特别的那个，帮助拼读，不是词源。

abstract.en: Picture a spotlight landing on one singer in a dark choir.
abstract.cn: 画面：聚光灯落在黑暗合唱团中的一位歌手身上。

abstract.en: Feel the teacher holding up one page among a stack of essays.
abstract.cn: 动作：老师从一摞作文里单独举起一页。

abstract.en: Taste the one dish you remember from a whole banquet.
abstract.cn: 感觉：整桌宴席中只记得的那一道菜。

examples.en: I like fruit, especially watermelon in summer.
examples.cn: 我喜欢水果，尤其是夏天的西瓜。

examples.en: This seat was kept especially for our teacher.
examples.cn: 这个座位是特意为老师留的。

examples.en: The exam was especially hard this year.
examples.cn: 今年这次考试格外难。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一斯佩修」——一眼挑出修一个重点，谐音帮助拼读，不是词源。

root: especially 由 special（拉丁 species「种类、外形」派生）加副词后缀 -ly 构成，字面即「以特别的方式」。species、specimen、specific 同根。

sensesIntro.en: Especially moves from singling out one in a group, to meaning very much, to doing something for one purpose.
sensesIntro.cn: especially 从群体中单挑一个，到程度「非常」，再到「特意为某目的」，义项层层聚焦。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a spotlight picking one out of a crowd.
core.cn: 核心意象：聚光灯从一群中挑出一个。

branches.cn: 大家都累，尤其是小男孩。
especially good、especially hard，意为非常。
特意为某人制作或购买。
「被单独挑出」使两种用法皆成立。
被挑出之物值得关注。

intro.en: Especially is built visibly on special plus -ly, and the species family stands behind it.
intro.cn: especially 由 special 加 -ly 清晰构成，背后是 species 词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin species 'kind, appearance' is the shared ancestor of this family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 species「种类、外形」是这一词族的共同祖先。

items.example: Inspect means to look into.
A special day is set apart from others.
items.exampleCN: special day 指与众不同的日子。

items.example: especially means in a special way.
Species is the Latin source word.
Specific details are singled out.
items.exampleCN: specific 指被明确挑出的细节。

items.example: A specimen shows its kind.
Specially made means custom made.
A specialist focuses on one kind of case.
items.exampleCN: 专科医生专注一类病例。

definition_zh: 甚至；连；更加；平的；偶数的；均匀的
definition_en: used to stress something surprising; also level, equal, or divisible by two
core_image: 水平的天平：两边一样高，甚至把另一边压得更低
scene: 天平左盘放着一摞书，右盘再加一枚硬币就平了。Add one more coin and the scale will be even.
sceneCN: 这里 even 是「平的、相等的」（第 3 个义项：两边持平）；句意是再加一枚硬币天平就平了。

derivatives.zh: 由 even 加 -ly 构成，义为「均匀地；平坦地」
由 even 加 -ness 构成，义为「平坦；均匀；平静」
拼写相近但词源不同，义为「晚上」，需注意区分

senses.title: Used to stress something surprising
senses.definition: used before a surprising word or fact to emphasize it
senses.definitionCN: 放在令人意外的词或事实前加强语气
senses.example: Even the teacher could not answer the question.
senses.exampleCN: 连老师都答不出这个问题。
senses.why: The word comes from a root meaning level, and stressing works by pushing the expectation even lower or further.
senses.whyCN: 词根本义是「平」，强调的手法是把预期再压低、推得更远。

senses.title: Still more, comparative force
senses.definition: used before a comparative to add extra force
senses.definitionCN: 放在比较级前加强比较
senses.example: The second film was even better than the first.
senses.exampleCN: 第二部电影比第一部还要好看。
senses.why: If two things already sit on a slope, even tips the balance further toward one side.
senses.whyCN: 两物已在斜坡上，even 再把天平向一边压。

senses.title: Level, smooth or equal
senses.definition: flat, regular, or equal in amount, height or quality
senses.definitionCN: 平坦、规则，或在量、高度、质上相等
senses.example: Make sure the floor is even before laying the tiles.
senses.exampleCN: 铺瓷砖前要确保地面平整。
senses.why: This is the original meaning: two edges that sit at the same height.
senses.whyCN: 这是本义：两条边处于同一高度。

senses.title: Divisible by two
senses.definition: of a number, able to be divided exactly by two
senses.definitionCN: 一个数能被二整除
senses.example: Two, four and six are even numbers.
senses.exampleCN: 二、四、六是偶数。
senses.why: Numbers paired off equally, like two matched sides of a balance, are called even.
senses.whyCN: 数能两两配对，如天平相等的两边，故称 even。

intro.en: Even is an Old English word meaning level or equal. The surprising-force use grew out of the image of pushing a balance further down.
intro.cn: even 是古英语词，本义「平、相等」。表示「甚至」的用法由「把天平再压下」的画面生长出来。

items.en: Old English efn meant 'level, equal, flat', the physical sense of matching heights.
items.cn: 古英语 efn 意为「平的、相等的、平坦的」，指高度相等的物理状态。

items.en: Middle English even kept the level sense and named numbers that pair off equally.
items.cn: 中古英语 even 保留「平」义，并用来称呼两两相配的偶数。

items.en: The adverb even appeared in the sense 'exactly, just', as in even now.
items.cn: 副词 even 出现「正是、恰恰」义，如 even now。

items.en: The stressing use, even the teacher, grew from pushing a comparison further than expected.
items.cn: 强调用法 even the teacher 源自把比较推得超出预期。

items.en: Even out and get even with extended the balance image into smoothing and repayment.
items.cn: even out 与 get even with 把天平意象延伸为抹平与扯平。

note.en: The first group collects look-alikes that only share spelling; the second collects near meanings about equality and stress.
note.cn: 第一组收集仅拼写相近的词；第二组收集与「相等、强调」相关的近义词。

entries.definition: the time before night; only shares the first letters, different root entirely
entries.definitionCN: 晚上；傍晚。仅开头拼写相同，词源完全不同。

entries.definition: something that happens; shares even- spelling from a Latin root, not related in meaning
entries.definitionCN: 事件。前缀拼写来自拉丁语，与「平」义无关。

entries.definition: the number 7; ends with the same letters by accident
entries.definitionCN: 七。词尾字母偶合，词源无关。

entries.definition: used like even to add surprise: still more, still worse
entries.definitionCN: 仍然；更加。与 even 同样可加强比较级。

entries.definition: level and smooth, close to the original physical sense
entries.definitionCN: 平的；扁平的。接近本义的物理「平」。

entries.definition: the same in size or amount, overlapping with even in equality uses
entries.definitionCN: 相等的。与 even 在「相等」义上重叠。

normalIntro.en: Five concrete hooks built from the real level root and classroom sentences.
normalIntro.cn: 五条基于「平」词根与课堂例句的具体联想。

normal.en: Learn even if first: it opens almost every concessive sentence.
normal.cn: even if＝即使，写作让步句最常用，先记短语。

normal.en: Even numbers pair off by two: two, four, six are level pairs.
normal.cn: even number 偶数：二、四、六，两两配对才「平」。

normal.en: Even better before a comparative adds real force.
normal.cn: even better 甚至更好：比较级前加 even 更有力。

normal.en: Even out returns the word to its original level meaning.
normal.cn: even out 把不平的东西抹平，回到本义。

normal.en: The sound hints at splitting even one coin equally, for spelling only.
normal.cn: 谐音：「一文钱也要平分」——连一文也要均分，帮助拼读，不是词源。

abstract.en: Picture two pans hanging at exactly the same height.
abstract.cn: 画面：天平两盘悬在同一高度。

abstract.en: Push one pan down further than anyone expected; that is even.
abstract.cn: 动作：把一盘压到超出所有人预期的低。

abstract.en: Feel a freshly ironed sheet, smooth without a single fold.
abstract.cn: 感觉：刚熨平的床单，平整无褶。

examples.en: Even a child can open this bottle.
examples.cn: 连小孩都能打开这个瓶子。

examples.en: Today is even colder than yesterday.
examples.cn: 今天比昨天还要冷。

examples.en: Eight is an even number.
examples.cn: 八是偶数。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一「文」」——一文钱也要平分，谐音帮助拼读，不是词源。

root: even 源自古英语 efn「平的、相等的」，是纯粹的日耳曼语词，与 evening「晚上」、event「事件」词源无关，拼写相近纯属巧合。

sensesIntro.en: Even runs from physical evenness, to even numbers, to the stress words even if and even better.
sensesIntro.cn: even 从物理的「平」，到偶数，再到 even if 与 even better 的强调用法，义项由实转虚。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a balance with both pans at the same height.
core.cn: 核心意象：两盘等高的天平。

branches.cn: 平整的地面与均匀的表面。
能被二整除配对的偶数。
连老师都答不出的强调用法。
even better，比之前还要好。
把差异抹平直至均匀。

intro.en: Even is a single Germanic word; its useful parts are phrases like even out rather than prefixes.
intro.cn: even 是单个日耳曼语词，其构词体现于 even out 等短语而非前后缀。

items.exampleCN: 古英语 efn 是直接祖先。

items.example: Spread the butter evenly.
The evenness of the road matters for cycling.
items.exampleCN: 路面的平整对骑车很重要。

items.example: Prices even out after the rush.
items.exampleCN: 抢购过后价格趋于平稳。

items.example: He wanted to get even with the bully.
It was raining; even so, we went out.
items.exampleCN: 下着雨，即便如此我们还是出门了。

items.example: Even if it rains, the match continues.
items.exampleCN: 即使下雨，比赛照常进行。

items.example: Event shares spelling but not the root.
items.exampleCN: event 仅拼写相近，词根不同。

definition_zh: 晚上；傍晚；黄昏
definition_en: the time between the end of the afternoon and bedtime
core_image: 日落后的长椅：天色渐暗、灯刚亮起的那段时光
scene: 放学后天边染上橘色，操场的人慢慢散了。We played football in the cool evening after class.
sceneCN: 这里 evening 是「晚上、傍晚」（第 1 个义项：下午结束到就寝前的时光）；句意是放学后我们在凉爽的傍晚踢球。

derivatives.zh: 复数词用作副词，义为「（在）每天晚上」
同根旧词，义为「前夜；前夕」
复合词，义为「晚礼服」

senses.title: The time before night
senses.definition: the period between the end of the day's work or school and bedtime
senses.definitionCN: 一天的工作或放学结束到就寝之间的时段
senses.example: The family watches TV together in the evening.
senses.exampleCN: 一家人晚上一起看电视。
senses.why: The Old English root ae meaning time is close to ever, so evening is the drawing-toward time of day.
senses.whyCN: 古英语词根接近 ever「渐近」，evening 即一天中渐渐走向结束的时光。

senses.title: A pleasant social time or event
senses.definition: a social occasion or enjoyable time spent in the evening, often in phrases like a lovely evening
senses.definitionCN: 晚间的社交场合或愉快经历，如 a lovely evening
senses.example: We spent a lovely evening at my aunt's house.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在姑姑家度过了一个愉快的夜晚。
senses.why: The stretch of time is filled with company, so the word names the occasion itself.
senses.whyCN: 这段时间被聚会填满，于是词义指那场聚会本身。

senses.title: The late part of something
senses.definition: the last or declining part of a period of life or history
senses.definitionCN: 生命或历史的最后、衰落阶段
senses.example: He wrote his best poems in the evening of his life.
senses.exampleCN: 他在人生的暮年写出了最好的诗。
senses.why: A day ends at evening, so a life's ending borrows the same closing light.
senses.whyCN: 一天在傍晚结束，人生的尽头便借用同样的收暮之光。

intro.en: Evening comes from Old English meaning the time when day draws to its close. It shares an ancient root with ever, both about becoming or drawing near.
intro.cn: evening 来自古英语，指白昼走向结束的时光。它与 ever 共享古老词根，都关于「渐变、临近」。

items.en: The root aefen named the close of day, related to a word meaning 'becoming, drawing near'.
items.cn: 古英语词根 aefen 指白昼将尽，与一个表示「渐成、临近」的词相关。

items.en: Aefening was formed with the -ing suffix, meaning the time of drawing to a close.
items.cn: aefening 加 -ing 后缀构成，意为「走向结束的时光」。

items.en: Middle English evenen and evening settled the modern spelling by the fifteenth century.
items.cn: 中古英语 evenen 与 evening 到十五世纪定型为现代拼写。

items.en: Good evening became the standard greeting as lamps and street life extended night activity.
items.cn: 随着灯火与夜生活延长，good evening 成为标准问候语。

items.en: The figurative use, the evening of one's life, is recorded from the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 比喻用法「人生的暮年」最早见于十七世纪的记录。

note.en: The first group collects look-alikes that are not related in root; the second collects near meanings about late-day time.
note.cn: 第一组收集词根无关的形近词；第二组收集与「晚间时段」相关的近义词。

entries.definition: level or even-numbered; shares letters by pure chance, different Germanic root
entries.definitionCN: 平的；偶数的。拼写偶合，词根完全不同。

entries.definition: something that happens, from Latin; only the opening letters match
entries.definitionCN: 事件。源自拉丁语，仅开头拼写相近。

entries.definition: the number 7; ends with the same letters by accident
entries.definitionCN: 七。词尾字母偶合，词源无关。

entries.definition: the darker moment just before night, shorter than evening
entries.definitionCN: 黄昏；暮色。比 evening 更短促、更暗。

entries.definition: the moment night begins
entries.definitionCN: 黄昏降临；夜幕降临时分。指夜开始的那一点。

entries.definition: the dark hours after sunset, longer and later than evening
entries.definitionCN: 夜晚。比 evening 更晚更长，指整个黑夜。

normalIntro.en: Five concrete hooks built from the real root, greetings and daily phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 五条基于真实词根、问候语与日常搭配的具体联想。

normal.en: Evening and ever share one old root: the sky draws near to night.
normal.cn: evening 与 ever 同根：天色「渐暗渐近」夜的时刻。

normal.en: Good evening greets; good night says goodbye and sleep.
normal.cn: Good evening 见面问候；Good night 道别安睡，一迎一别。

normal.en: In the evening is general; on Sunday evening names one night.
normal.cn: in the evening 泛指晚上；on Sunday evening 指具体某晚。

normal.en: Eve means the night before: Christmas Eve is a famous one.
normal.cn: eve 是前夜，Christmas Eve 平安夜，同根同源。

normal.en: The sound hints at an evening breeze, for spelling only.
normal.cn: 谐音：「一服晚风」——傍晚迎着晚风，帮助拼读，不是词源。

abstract.en: Picture an orange sky over a quiet school playground after class.
abstract.cn: 画面：放学后橘色天空罩着安静的操场。

abstract.en: Feel street lamps blinking on one by one as the sky darkens.
abstract.cn: 动作：天色变暗，路灯一盏盏亮起。

abstract.en: Hear the day's last sounds softening into quiet.
abstract.cn: 感觉：一天的声音渐渐归于安静。

examples.en: In the evening we do homework and read books.
examples.cn: 晚上我们做作业和看书。

examples.en: Good evening, welcome to our school open day.
examples.cn: 晚上好，欢迎来到我们学校的开放日。

examples.en: They spent a quiet evening by the river.
examples.cn: 他们在河边度过了一个安静的夜晚。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一服晚风」——傍晚迎着晚风，谐音帮助拼读，不是词源。

root: evening 来自古英语 aefening（aefen「傍晚」+ -ing），与 ever「永远」共享表示「渐变、临近」的日耳曼词根，与 even「平的」词源无关。

sensesIntro.en: Evening runs from the late-day hours, to a pleasant social time, to the closing stage of life or history.
sensesIntro.cn: evening 从傍晚时段，到愉快的夜晚聚会，再到人生或历史的末期，义项由时到事到喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the orange hour when day leans toward its close.
core.cn: 核心意象：白昼倾向结束的橘色时刻。

branches.cn: 放学后做作业与家人相处的常规傍晚时段。
与朋友家人共度的愉快夜晚。
人生暮年，安静而晚的阶段。
灯光点亮、引人相聚的时分。
借暮色之光泛指一切结束。

intro.en: Evening is built with the Old English -ing suffix on the aefen root; its kin are time words, not Latin.
intro.cn: evening 由古英语 aefen 词根加 -ing 后缀构成，同族词是时间词而非拉丁词。

items.example: Aefen is the direct ancestor of eve and evening.
items.exampleCN: aefen 是 eve 与 evening 的直接祖先。

items.example: Aefening means the aefen time.
items.exampleCN: aefening 指 aefen 的时段。

items.example: New Year's Eve comes before the new year.
items.exampleCN: New Year's Eve 在新年之前。

items.example: She works evenings at the library.
Ever and evening share the root of becoming.
items.exampleCN: ever 与 evening 共享「渐成」词根。

items.example: Nightfall is a compound of night and fall.
items.exampleCN: nightfall 由 night 和 fall 复合。

items.example: Good evening opens a formal night event.
items.exampleCN: good evening 用于晚间正式场合开场。

items.example: Evening dress is worn to balls and operas.
items.exampleCN: 晚礼服用于舞会与歌剧。

definition_zh: 曾经；从来；在任何时候；永远；究竟（用于强调）
definition_en: at any time; always; used for emphasis in questions and negatives
core_image: 无限延伸的时间线：任何一点都算数
scene: 爷爷翻着旧相册说这是他见过最亮的星空。It was the brightest star he had ever seen.
sceneCN: 这里 ever 是「曾经」（第 1 个义项：在任何时候）；句意是他从未见过这么亮的星。

derivatives.zh: 由 ever 加 green 构成，义为「常绿树；常绿的」
由 ever 加 lasting 构成，义为「永恒的；持久的」
由 how 加 ever 构成，义为「然而；无论如何」

senses.title: At any time
senses.definition: at any time, used especially in questions and negative sentences
senses.definitionCN: 在任何时候，尤用于疑问句与否定句
senses.example: Have you ever visited the Great Wall?
senses.exampleCN: 你曾经游览过长城吗？
senses.why: The Old English root means always, so the question sweeps across the whole timeline.
senses.whyCN: 古英语词根意为「永远」，疑问因此扫过整条时间线。

senses.title: Always, continually
senses.definition: all the time, or again and again, often in ever since or for ever
senses.definitionCN: 一直，或一次次，常见于 ever since 与 for ever
senses.example: We have been friends ever since primary school.
senses.exampleCN: 我们从小学起一直是朋友。
senses.why: When the sweep never ends, the any-time word hardens into an always word.
senses.whyCN: 当扫掠没有终点，「任何时刻」便固化为「一直」。

senses.title: Used for emphasis
senses.definition: used after words like what, how or why to add surprise or force
senses.definitionCN: 放在 what、how、why 等词后加强惊讶或力度
senses.example: Why ever did you hide the keys there?
senses.exampleCN: 你究竟为什么把钥匙藏在那里？
senses.why: Stretching the timeline wide makes any answer seem astonishing.
senses.whyCN: 把时间线拉到最宽，任何答案都显得惊人。

senses.title: Comparative reinforcement
senses.definition: used after superlatives to mean at any time so far
senses.definitionCN: 用在最高级后表示迄今为止任何时候
senses.example: It was the best meal we had ever cooked.
senses.exampleCN: 那是我们做过的最好的一餐。
senses.why: The best of all time is found by sweeping every moment once.
senses.whyCN: 把每一时刻都扫一遍，才能选出有史以来最佳。

intro.en: Ever is an Old English compound of ae meaning ever and a related root for time, literally 'always in time'. It is the same root family as evening.
intro.cn: ever 是古英语复合词，意为「在任何时候」，与 evening 同属「渐成、时间」词族。

items.en: Old English aefre meant 'ever, at any time', built from roots about time and becoming.
items.cn: 古英语 aefre 意为「永远、任何时候」，由关于时间与渐成的词根构成。

items.en: Middle English ever spread into questions, negatives and emphatic phrases.
items.cn: 中古英语 ever 扩展到疑问句、否定句与强调短语。

items.en: Ever since and for ever became fixed phrases in this period.
items.cn: ever since 与 for ever 在这一时期成为固定短语。

items.en: Compound adjectives like ever-growing and evergreen kept the sense of continuation.
items.cn: ever-growing 与 evergreen 等复合词保留了延续之意。

items.en: The emphatic use, why ever not, became common in spoken English.
items.cn: 强调用法 why ever not 在英语口语中变得常用。

note.en: The first group collects the ever-compound family; the second collects near meanings about time.
note.cn: 第一组收集 ever 复合词族；第二组收集与时间相关的近义词。

entries.definition: each one of a group; historically a fusion of ever plus each
entries.definitionCN: 每一个。历史上由 ever 与 each 融合而来，形近义异。

entries.definition: the late-day time; a true cousin sharing the old root of becoming
entries.definitionCN: 晚上；同根真表亲，共享「渐成」词根。

entries.definition: to cut off; only the letters resemble, root is Latin
entries.definitionCN: 切断。仅拼写相似，词根是拉丁语。

entries.definition: at all times, the plain everyday word for continuity
entries.definitionCN: 总是。表示持续的朴素日常词。

entries.definition: at no time; the direct opposite in the same shape
entries.definitionCN: 从不。同构形的直接反义词。

entries.definition: one time at some point in the past
entries.definitionCN: 曾经一次。只指过去的某一次。

normalIntro.en: Five concrete hooks built from real phrases and question patterns.
normalIntro.cn: 五条基于真实短语与疑问句式的具体联想。

normal.en: Have you ever is the classic present perfect question opener.
normal.cn: Have you ever...? 是最经典的现在完成时问句开头。

normal.en: Ever since means from then until now, with perfect tenses.
normal.cn: ever since＝从那以后一直，常配完成时。

normal.en: Hardly ever means almost never; it contrasts with always.
normal.cn: hardly ever 几乎从不，与 always 成对对比记忆。

normal.en: An evergreen stays green year after year.
normal.cn: evergreen 常绿树：ever＋green，绿了一年又一年。

normal.en: The sound hints at love counted at any time, for spelling only.
normal.cn: 谐音：「爱我」——爱在任何时刻都算数，帮助拼读，不是词源。

abstract.en: Picture a timeline stretching to both edges of the paper.
abstract.cn: 画面：一条延伸到纸两端的无限时间线。

abstract.en: Sweep your hand across all the marks on that line.
abstract.cn: 动作：手掌扫过线上所有刻度。

abstract.en: Feel a friendship that keeps going past every season.
abstract.cn: 感觉：跨越每个季节仍在延续的友谊。

examples.en: Have you ever ridden a horse?
examples.cn: 你骑过马吗？

examples.en: I have hardly ever seen him angry.
examples.cn: 我几乎从没见过他生气。

examples.en: This is the tallest tower ever built in our city.
examples.cn: 这是我市有史以来建成的最高塔。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱「我」」——爱在任何时刻都算数，谐音帮助拼读，不是词源。

root: ever 来自古英语 aefre，由表示「时间、渐成」的日耳曼词根构成，与 evening、every 同族；与拉丁词根无关。

sensesIntro.en: Ever sweeps the whole timeline: any time, all the time, and the surprising time behind an emphatic question.
sensesIntro.cn: ever 扫过整条时间线：任何时候、一直如此、以及疑问中令人惊奇的某一刻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand sweeping across an endless timeline.
core.cn: 核心意象：手掌扫过无限延伸的时间线。

branches.cn: 疑问与否定句：have you ever。
ever since 与 for ever，整条时间线一起看。
why ever、what ever，增添惊奇。
the best ever，从所有时点中选出。

definition_zh: 每一个；每个；所有的；每隔
definition_en: each one of a group without exception; all
core_image: 点名册：一个不落地挨个勾选
scene: 早读前班长把点名册挨个勾完，全班到齐。Every student in our class passed the spelling test.
sceneCN: 这里 every 是「每一个、所有的」（第 1 个义项：无一例外）；句意是我们班每个学生都通过了拼写测验。

derivatives.zh: 由 every 加 one 构成，义为「每个人」

senses.title: Each one without exception
senses.definition: each single one of a group, taken one by one
senses.definitionCN: 一群中的每一个，逐个看待
senses.example: Every desk was cleaned before the holiday.
senses.exampleCN: 放假前每一张桌子都被擦干净了。
senses.why: The word grew out of ever plus each, so it walks the line tick by tick.
senses.whyCN: 该词由 ever 与 each 融合而来，像沿刻度逐个走过。

senses.title: All together, with singular force
senses.definition: all of a group considered together, though the noun stays singular
senses.definitionCN: 全体一起看待，但名词仍用单数
senses.example: Every member agreed with the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 所有成员都同意这个计划。
senses.why: One-by-one checking ends in a full house, so the meaning reaches all without losing the singular frame.
senses.whyCN: 逐个检查的结果是全员到齐，词义覆盖全体而仍持单数框架。

senses.title: At regular intervals
senses.definition: used with numbers to show how often something happens, as in every two days
senses.definitionCN: 与数字连用表示频率，如 every two days
senses.example: The bus comes every ten minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 公交车每十分钟来一班。
senses.why: Marching one by one at a fixed pace turns checking into rhythm.
senses.whyCN: 按固定步幅逐个行进，检查便化为节律。

intro.en: Every is a Middle English fusion of ever and each. Its image is checking a group one by one, without missing a single one.
intro.cn: every 是中古英语 ever 与 each 的融合词，画面是逐个清点、一个不漏。

items.en: The roots aefre (ever) and aelc (each) both existed in Old English before the fusion.
items.cn: 古英语中 aefre（ever）与 aelc（each）在融合前已并存。

items.en: The fused form everich appeared in the thirteenth century, later shortened to every.
items.cn: 十三世纪出现融合形式 everich，后缩略为 every。

items.en: Chaucer used everich and every side by side in his poems.
items.cn: 乔叟的诗中 everich 与 every 并用。

items.en: The pronouns everyone, everybody and everything formed from every in this era.
items.cn: 代词 everyone、everybody、everything 在这一时期由 every 构成。

items.en: The interval use, every ten minutes, became standard for time and measures.
items.cn: 间隔用法 every ten minutes 成为时间与度量的标准表达。

note.en: The first group collects the fused-family forms; the second collects near meanings about each and all.
note.cn: 第一组收集融合词族的成员；第二组收集与「每个、全部」相关的近义词。

entries.definition: every person; it and everybody share the meaning
entries.definitionCN: 每个人。与 everybody 同义，可互换。

entries.definition: every person, more spoken and friendly in tone

entries.definition: considered one by one, works with two or more
entries.definitionCN: 每个（逐个）。可用于两者以上，逐个视角更强。

entries.definition: the whole group together, takes plural nouns
entries.definitionCN: 全部。整体视角，接复数名词。

entries.definition: an emphatic phrase meaning absolutely each one
entries.definitionCN: 每一个（强调）。固定强调短语。

normal.cn: every＝ever（任何时候）＋each（每个），融合词一个不漏。

abstract.cn: 动作：沿储物柜逐个走过并逐一触碰。

abstract.cn: 感觉：节拍器以完全规律的间隔敲击。

examples.cn: 每天早晨她给阳台上的花浇水。

examples.cn: 图书馆除周一外每天开放。

examples.cn: 每个学生考试都必须带铅笔。
